# Gauntlet — Iteration 01

**Subject:** Tiger I Ausf. H, Henschel, late February 1943 — hull only
**Suite:** 175 tests passing, `GAUNTLET_EXIT=0`, 17,888 triangles
**Views:** `docs/gauntlet/renders/` — five orthographic, four three-quarter, five silhouettes, four details
**Numerical QA:** `docs/gauntlet/numerical-qa.md`, generated by the test suite

---

## Verdict

# REJECT

Two critical faults were found and corrected during this iteration. A third
class of finding — absent subsystems — is what the verdict actually turns on:
four of the six critics have nothing in front of them to assess.

The model is a hull. It has no turret, no gun, no suspension, no tracks, no
hatch lids, no track guards and no exterior fittings. A reconstruction in that
state cannot pass a historical-accuracy review, because most of what makes a
Tiger recognisable as a Tiger is not present to be judged.

This is not a formality. Both critical faults below were found by looking at
renders of the hull against references and by measuring built geometry — the
same procedures, applied to subsystems that do not yet exist, would find
nothing. Passing this iteration would mean certifying an absence.

---

## Critical findings

### CRITICAL-1 — The hull was built as its own mirror image · CORRECTED

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reference** | Every head-on photograph of a Tiger I: driver front left, radio operator and hull machine gun front right. Viewed from the front the ball mount appears on the viewer's left. |
| **Model** | The ball mount appeared on the viewer's right and the driver's visor on the left. The driver's and radio operator's roof hatches were likewise transposed, as was the commander's cupola in the turret spec. |
| **Difference** | The entire vehicle was laterally reflected. |
| **Severity** | Critical |

**Cause.** `src/spec/units.ts` documented `+X` as starboard. In a right-handed
frame with `+Y` up and `+Z` forward, the vehicle's own starboard is
`forward × up = -X`. Face north with `+Z` north and `+Y` up: `+X` comes out
west, and your right hand points east. Every asymmetric feature was then
authored against the wrong reading.

**Why nothing caught it.** The error was in the shared assumption, so every test
and every builder inherited it and agreed with itself. A mirrored tank is
internally consistent, symmetric under its own symmetry tests, and dimensionally
perfect. It only fails against an external reference.

**Correction applied.** Laterality is now written by name rather than by sign:
`port()` and `starboard()` take a positive magnitude and place it.
`tests/spec/laterality.test.ts` re-derives starboard from the cross product
instead of reading the comment, then measures the built geometry rather than the
spec — a builder that negates X somewhere would satisfy a spec-only check and
still produce a mirrored tank. It distinguishes the visor from the machine gun
by aperture shape, probing 60 mm above each centre where the round bore is still
open and the 95 mm slot has closed; probing the centres alone passes on a
mirrored hull, because the two sit within 10 mm of the same height.

### CRITICAL-2 — The frontal armour was a single wedge · CORRECTED

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reference** | Jentz & Doyle, via Tank Encyclopedia: the front comprises a 100 mm lower front plate, **a short glacis 60 mm thick**, and a reclined 100 mm driver's plate. tiger1.info's welding description has the glacis welded above and below to the superstructure front plate, seated in a cut groove. |
| **Model** | The 100 mm nose ran directly into the 100 mm driver's plate as one continuous surface. The 60 mm plate existed, but had been placed above the driver's plate as a long front deck. |
| **Difference** | A structural member absent from its structural position. |
| **Severity** | Critical |

**Raised by the project owner**, twice, before the gauntlet found it. That is
itself a finding: the review procedure in place at the time did not look at the
front of the tank against a reference.

**Correction applied.** The front is rebuilt as four distinct planes. The
transition heights were then measured off the supplied 1:50 side elevation
rather than estimated — the drawing read pixel by pixel and calibrated two
independent ways, 20.3 mm/px on the sourced hull length and 19.8 mm/px on the
ground-to-roof height, agreeing to 2.6 per cent. That measurement moved the
nose-to-glacis transition from 980 mm to 1,150 mm and the glacis run from
400 mm to 550 mm.

`tests/parts/frontHull.test.ts` samples the front by ray casting and
differentiates the profile, so the wedge cannot return. The numerical QA table
measures the included angle at the step: **146°**, where a continuous wedge
reads 180°.

---

## Critic 1 — Historical accuracy · REJECT

Scope: does this match a Henschel Tiger I Ausf. H of late February 1943,
Fgst. ~250050–250100?

**What holds.** The configuration decisions in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md` are
correct for the date and are enforced by `src/spec/variants.ts`: Maybach HL 210
P45 (the HL 230 arrives at Fgst. 250251 in May 1943), 25 mm turret roof (40 mm
only from March 1944), TZF 9b binocular sight and therefore two mantlet
apertures, Feifel air pre-cleaners fitted, drum cupola, 18-bolt road wheel rims,
no return rollers.

**Findings.**

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 1.1 | The vehicle was mirrored — see CRITICAL-1. | Critical, corrected |
| 1.2 | The frontal armour arrangement was wrong — see CRITICAL-2. | Critical, corrected |
| 1.3 | Interlocking plate teeth are absent from every joint. Tiger hull plates were stepped and interlocked before welding. They were removed in an earlier stage after a one-sided implementation put 50 mm of steel below the belly line, and have not been reinstated. | Major |
| 1.4 | Hatch lateral position (±560 mm) is `estimated` from a photograph, not measured. Plan drawings suggest the crew hatches sit further outboard. | Minor |
| 1.5 | 82 spec values remain at `confidence: 'estimated'`. The register in `docs/UNCERTAINTY.md` lists 12 open questions, of which #2 (turret ring clear opening) blocks the turret and the interior outright. | Major |

**REJECT.** 1.3 and 1.5 are unresolved, and the configuration is verifiable only
for the fraction of the vehicle that exists.

## Critic 2 — Hull geometry · REJECT

Scope: are the plates real, correctly thick, correctly angled, correctly joined?

**What holds.** Every plate is a genuine closed solid built by the `plate()`
primitive, with apertures as hole polygons in the outline rather than CSG
booleans — so interior surfaces are real back faces and a hatch aperture is a
real hole. Manifold audits, signed-volume checks, ray-march thickness
measurement and symmetry tests all pass. The numerical QA table is measured, not
asserted:

- Hull length nose to rear plate: **6,317 mm** against a sourced 6,316 mm
- Hull roof height: **1,780 mm**, exact
- Ground clearance under the belly: **475 mm** against 470 mm
- Nose, glacis and driver's plate thicknesses: **100 / 60 / 100 mm**, exact
- Nose and driver's plate rake: **25°** and **9°**, in opposite directions

**Findings.**

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 2.1 | The frontal wedge — see CRITICAL-2. The standing rule for this critic was to reject immediately on finding it. | Critical, corrected |
| 2.2 | The exhaust stacks and the Feifel canisters interpenetrated by 145 mm. Authored in separate sittings against separate references; each individually plausible, and neither one's tests knew the other existed. Stacks moved inboard from 900 mm to 700 mm; `tests/parts/rearClash.test.ts` now checks fittings that share a plate against each other. | Major, corrected |
| 2.3 | The Feifel trunking arched 335 mm above the roof, because `trunkRise` served as both the resting height on the deck and an extra crest on top of it. In the photographs the trunking is a low hump. The crest is gone; peak now 217 mm. | Major, corrected |
| 2.4 | The Feifel trunk terminated in mid-deck with an open end, connecting to nothing, because the engine deck's air intake was not modelled. The plan view shows the drum plainly, with both trunks converging on it; it now exists and they reach it. | Major, corrected |
| 2.5 | No hatch lids. The driver's and radio operator's lids are now built, seated in their rings on pivot posts, and open. The engine hatch is still an aperture with nothing in it. | Major, partly corrected |
| 2.6 | No track guards, tow points, headlights or S-mine dischargers. All four are now built; spare-track brackets, tools and tow cables remain absent. | Major, partly corrected |
| 2.7 | Only two radiator grilles, one a side. The 1:50 plan view shows FOUR — a long forward grille and a shorter aft one on each side, fore and aft of a small access panel. Half the engine deck was blank. | Major, corrected |
| 2.8 | `MaterialId` was `string`, so a misspelt material fell through to the debug fallback and rendered magenta with nothing failing. It shipped a bright pink track guard. The type is now derived from the preset table. | Major, corrected |

**REJECT** on 2.4 through 2.6. The armour envelope itself would pass.

## Critic 3 — Turret and gun · REJECT

**Nothing to assess.** No turret, no cupola, no mantlet, no 8.8 cm KwK 36. The
turret spec exists and is partly sourced; no geometry has been built.

Blocked on `UNCERTAINTY #2`: the turret ring clear opening is quoted as 1,830 mm
throughout the secondary literature without attribution. tiger1.info gives the
bearing outer diameter (2,100 mm) and the ball circle (1,990 mm) but not the
clear opening. That figure sets the turret basket, which sets crew station
spacing, which sets the whole fighting compartment — building on it unverified
risks a cascade.

Also blocked on `UNCERTAINTY #3` (elevation limits: −6.5°/+17° versus −8°/+15°,
both in wide circulation) and `UNCERTAINTY #4` (mantlet thickness, where sources
quote 100–200 mm without stating where it is measured).

**REJECT.**

## Critic 4 — Running gear · REJECT

**Nothing to assess.** No road wheels, no torsion bars, no swing arms, no
sprockets, no idlers, no track links.

The specification is in place and cross-checks arithmetically: a 20-tooth
sprocket at 130 mm pitch gives a derived pitch radius of 415.55 mm against an
independently sourced outer radius of 457.2 mm, and the 41.65 mm difference is a
plausible tooth-tip and guide-horn allowance.

`UNCERTAINTY #9` remains open: which of the three interleave rows each station's
wheels occupy is held as data rather than code, so a correction is a spec edit,
but it is not yet sourced from a drawing.

**REJECT.**

## Critic 5 — Visual quality · REJECT

**What holds.** Materials are fully procedural — no texture files — driven by
four custom vertex attributes (`aEdgeDist`, `aCavity`, `aWear`, `aRegion`).
Weld beads are irregular and are excluded from the symmetry test by a
counterpart test that asserts they *are* irregular. The scene is verifiably lit:
a guard test reads framebuffer pixels, after an earlier NaN environment probe
silently blackened every lit surface.

**Findings.**

| # | Finding | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| 5.1 | The procedural noise reads as speckle rather than as steel at plan-view scale. The frequency is tuned for close inspection and does not hold up at distance. | Major |
| 5.2 | The front and rear plates carry a blue-grey cast inconsistent with the rest of the hull. | Minor |
| 5.3 | The Feifel trunking renders as near-black with no highlight, reading as a flat silhouette rather than as a curved metal duct. | Minor |
| 5.4 | Edge treatment is uneven — this is deferred work under acceptance criterion **R3**, "polish up the edges once ur done", and is correctly not yet started. | Deferred |

**REJECT** on 5.1.

## Critic 6 — Reference match · REJECT

Scope: the rendered model set directly against the supplied drawing and
photographs.

| Feature | Reference | Model | Difference | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hull machine gun side | Viewer's left, head-on | Was viewer's right | Mirrored | Critical, corrected |
| Frontal plate count | Nose, short glacis, driver's plate | Was a single wedge | One plate absent | Critical, corrected |
| Roof front edge behind nose top | ~670 mm, measured off the 1:50 drawing | 634 mm | −36 mm, inside the drawing's 20 mm/px resolution | Acceptable |
| Hull length to width | Drawing side and plan views | Within 1 mm on length, 18 mm on width | — | Acceptable |
| Rear deck trunking profile | A low hump over the rear deck | Was a 335 mm arch | Corrected to 217 mm | Major, corrected |
| Overall silhouette | Tank | Hull only | No turret, gun, tracks or running gear | Critical |

On the last row the comparison cannot proceed. The supplied photographs show
complete vehicles; the model's silhouette is missing everything above the roof
line and everything below the sponsons.

**A limit worth stating plainly.** The 1:50 drawing resolves gross proportions
and the position of major transitions. It cannot resolve a 60 mm plate — three
pixels — or a ten-degree slope, which is inside the dithering noise. Plate
thicknesses and angles therefore come from Jentz & Doyle; only transition
heights come from the drawing. One trap it set: the front track guard projects
forward of the nose as a thin separate edge, so reading the outline as "leftmost
ink per row" tracks the guard rather than the armour and suggests a vertical
front face 600 mm tall.

**REJECT.**

## Required corrections before the next gauntlet

Ordered. Nothing below is optional.

1. ~~Reinstate interlocking teeth at every plate joint~~ — **deferred to the
   Stage 9 detail pass**, under acceptance criterion **R2**: *"try your best to
   detail the tank, AFTER youve finished everything"*. Verzahnung is a joint
   detail visible on close inspection, which is the category R2 defers. It stays
   a Major finding and stays open; it is the ordering that changes, not the
   requirement. The mechanism is a tenon-and-mortise pair — the side wall's
   teeth pass through mortises cut in the nose plate — and both halves must be
   generated from one shared joint definition so they cannot drift.
2. Hatch lids for the driver, radio operator and engine deck, on real hinges
   wired to dynamic collision (2.5).
3. Track guards with the January 1943 triangular ends, tow points, dual Bosch
   headlights, S-mine dischargers (2.6).
4. Engine deck air intake, so the Feifel trunking connects to something (2.4).
5. Resolve `UNCERTAINTY #2` or record its acceptance as reconstruction, then
   build the turret with five cupola vision slits as genuine apertures (Critic 3).
6. Retune the procedural noise so it holds at distance (5.1).
7. Running gear (Critic 4).

## Procedural changes carried forward

Both critical faults shared a shape: internally consistent, dimensionally
perfect, wrong against an external reference. The tests could not have caught
either, because the tests were written from the same assumption as the geometry.

- **Every claim of numerical accuracy is generated by a test.**
  `docs/gauntlet/numerical-qa.md` is written by `tests/parts/numericalQA.test.ts`
  and a row outside tolerance fails the suite. Writing it caught two of my own
  measurements being of the wrong thing — hull length read off the bounding box,
  which the Feifel overhang inflates, and roof height likewise, which whatever
  fitting stands tallest sets.
- **Fittings that share a plate are checked against each other**, not only
  against the plate (2.2).
- **A number does two jobs at your peril** (2.3).
- **Renders are evidence.** Chrome comes off every captured view, the cameras
  frame the subject, and the dimension envelope stays out of shot.
